# The 1D Ising Model: Exact Two-Point Spin Correlation Function and Exponential Decay

This file proves, from first principles (directly from the sum over spin
configurations), the classical exact formula for the **endpoint two-point
correlation function** of the open (free-boundary) one-dimensional Ising model:

  `⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ = (tanh (β J))ⁿ`,

together with its consequences: exponential decay of correlations with a finite
**correlation length** `ξ = 1 / g`, where `g = log(coth (β J))` is exactly the
transfer-matrix spectral gap, and convergence of the correlation to `0` at every
positive temperature (so long-range order is absent in 1D for all `T > 0`).

A configuration of a chain with `n` bonds (hence `n + 1` sites) is a function
`s : Fin (n+1) → Bool`, where a spin is `+1` (`true`) or `-1` (`false`) via `sp`.
The (nearest-neighbour, zero-field) Boltzmann weight of `s` is the product of the
edge factors `exp (β J σᵢ σᵢ₊₁)`.  We work with the *unnormalised* signed sum

  `corrNum β J n = ∑ s, sp (s 0) · sp (s (Fin.last n)) · weight s`,

so that `⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ = corrNum / Zfree`.

## Main results

* `corrNum_closed` — the exact unnormalised correlation
    `corrNum β J n = 2 * (2 * sinh (β J)) ^ n`,
  proved by a genuine induction over the chain (peel off site `0`), the signed
  analogue of the partition-function recursion.
* `corr_eq_tanh_pow` — the **headline exact correlation function**
    `corr β J n = (tanh (β J)) ^ n`.
* `corr_eq_exp_neg_gap` — the **exponential-decay form** for `β, J > 0`:
    `corr β J n = exp (-(spectralGap β J) * n)` with
    `spectralGap β J = log (cosh (β J)) - log (sinh (β J)) = log (coth (β J))`.
* `spectralGap_pos` — the gap (inverse correlation length) is strictly positive
  for every positive temperature.
* `corr_tendsto_zero` — `⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ → 0` as `n → ∞`: no long-range order in 1D at
  any positive temperature.

## Application keywords

statistical mechanics, Ising model, correlation function, correlation length,
exponential decay, spectral gap, transfer matrix, spin chain, probability

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypotheses explored in this research cycle:
  (H1) The unnormalised endpoint correlation has the closed form
       `corrNum = 2 (2 sinh βJ)^n` — the *signed* sibling of the partition
       function `Zfree = 2 (2 cosh βJ)^n`.                            [TARGET]
  (H2) The signed transfer recursion `corrNum (n+1) = (2 sinh βJ) · corrNum n`
       follows by peeling site 0 via `Fin.cons` and the single-bond identity
       `∑_b sp b · exp(βJ · sp b · y) = 2 · y · sinh βJ` (uses *oddness* of
       sinh, in contrast to the *evenness* of cosh used for `Zfree`).  [TARGET]
  (H3) Dividing by `Zfree` gives `⟨σ₀σₙ⟩ = (sinh/cosh)^n = (tanh βJ)^n`. [TARGET]
  (H4) For β,J>0, `tanh βJ ∈ (0,1)`, so `⟨σ₀σₙ⟩ = exp(-g n)` with
       `g = -log tanh βJ = log coth βJ > 0` (the spectral gap), and the
       correlation decays to 0: no 1D long-range order at any T>0.    [TARGET]
Insight:
  The 1D partition function is governed by the EVEN single-bond sum (cosh); the
  two-point function is governed by the ODD single-bond sum (sinh). Their ratio
  per bond is exactly `tanh βJ`, the eigenvalue ratio `λ₋/λ₊` of the transfer
  matrix, which is why the correlation length equals the inverse spectral gap.
-/
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators Topology
open Filter

namespace IsingCorrelation

/-- Spin value associated to a Boolean: `true ↦ +1`, `false ↦ -1`. -/
noncomputable def sp (b : Bool) : ℝ := if b then 1 else -1

/-- A spin times itself is `1`. -/
theorem sp_mul_self (b : Bool) : sp b * sp b = 1 := by
  cases b <;> simp [sp]

/-- The nearest-neighbour Boltzmann weight of a configuration `s` on a chain of
`n` bonds: the product of the edge factors `exp (β J σᵢ σᵢ₊₁)`. -/
noncomputable def weight (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Bool) : ℝ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, Real.exp (β * J * sp (s i.castSucc) * sp (s i.succ))

/-- The free-boundary partition function: sum of the Boltzmann weights. -/
noncomputable def Zfree (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ s : Fin (n + 1) → Bool, weight β J n s

/-- The *unnormalised* endpoint two-point correlation: the signed configuration
sum `∑ s, σ₀ σₙ · weight s`. -/
noncomputable def corrNum (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ s : Fin (n + 1) → Bool, sp (s 0) * sp (s (Fin.last n)) * weight β J n s

/-- The (normalised) endpoint two-point correlation `⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩`. -/
noncomputable def corr (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := corrNum β J n / Zfree β J n

/-! ### Partition function closed form (re-derived, self-contained) -/

/-- The single-bond *even* sum: `∑_b exp(c · sp b · sp y) = 2 cosh c`,
independent of the neighbouring spin `y` (parity of `cosh`). -/
theorem sum_bool_exp (c : ℝ) (y : Bool) :
    (∑ b : Bool, Real.exp (c * sp b * sp y)) = 2 * Real.cosh c := by
  rw [Fintype.sum_bool, Real.cosh_eq]
  cases y <;>
    · simp only [sp, if_true, if_false, Bool.false_eq_true, mul_one, mul_neg, neg_neg]
      ring

/-- The single-bond *odd* (signed) sum: `∑_b sp b · exp(c · sp b · sp y)
= 2 · sp y · sinh c` (oddness of `sinh`). -/
theorem sum_bool_sp_exp (c : ℝ) (y : Bool) :
    (∑ b : Bool, sp b * Real.exp (c * sp b * sp y)) = 2 * sp y * Real.sinh c := by
  rw [Fintype.sum_bool, Real.sinh_eq]
  cases y <;>
    simp only [sp, Bool.false_eq_true, if_true, if_false, mul_one, mul_neg, neg_neg,
      Real.exp_neg] <;>
    ring

/-- The Boltzmann weight factorises when prepending a spin `b` (peeling site `0`). -/
theorem weight_cons (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (b : Bool) (t : Fin (n + 1) → Bool) :
    weight β J (n + 1) (Fin.cons b t) =
      Real.exp (β * J * sp b * sp (t 0)) * weight β J n t := by
  unfold weight
  rw [Fin.prod_univ_succ]
  simp only [Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ, Fin.castSucc_zero]
  refine congrArg (Real.exp (β * J * sp b * sp (t 0)) * ·) ?_
  apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
  intro i _
  rw [← Fin.succ_castSucc, Fin.cons_succ]

/-- Transfer recursion for the partition function: `Z (n+1) = (2 cosh βJ) · Z n`. -/
theorem Zfree_succ (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    Zfree β J (n + 1) = (2 * Real.cosh (β * J)) * Zfree β J n := by
  unfold Zfree
  rw [← Equiv.sum_comp (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ => Bool)), Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_comm,
    Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro t _
  have h : ∀ b : Bool, (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ : Fin (n + 1 + 1) => Bool)) (b, t) = Fin.cons b t :=
    fun b => rfl
  simp_rw [h, weight_cons]
  rw [← Finset.sum_mul, sum_bool_exp]

/-- Exact closed form: `Zfree β J n = 2 (2 cosh (β J))ⁿ`. -/
theorem Zfree_closed (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    Zfree β J n = 2 * (2 * Real.cosh (β * J)) ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => unfold Zfree weight; simp
  | succ k ih => rw [Zfree_succ, ih, pow_succ]; ring

/-- Positivity of the partition function. -/
theorem Zfree_pos (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : 0 < Zfree β J n := by
  rw [Zfree_closed]
  have hc : 0 < Real.cosh (β * J) := Real.cosh_pos _
  positivity

/-! ### Two-point correlation closed form -/

/-- **Signed transfer recursion.** Peeling site `0`, the unnormalised correlation
satisfies `corrNum (n+1) = (2 sinh βJ) · corrNum n`. -/
theorem corrNum_succ (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    corrNum β J (n + 1) = (2 * Real.sinh (β * J)) * corrNum β J n := by
  unfold corrNum
  rw [← Equiv.sum_comp (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ => Bool)), Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_comm,
    Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro t _
  have h : ∀ b : Bool, (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ : Fin (n + 1 + 1) => Bool)) (b, t) = Fin.cons b t :=
    fun b => rfl
  have hlast : ∀ b : Bool,
      (Fin.cons b t : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → Bool) (Fin.last (n + 1)) = t (Fin.last n) := by
    in

# Future Directions — Statistical Mechanics: Ising Model Phase Transition

This cycle added `Catalog/Physics/IsingCorrelation.lean`, which proves from first
principles (directly from the configuration sum) the exact two-point correlation
function of the open 1D Ising chain, its exponential decay with correlation
length `ξ = 1/g` equal to the inverse transfer-matrix spectral gap
`g = log(coth βJ)`, the absence of long-range order at every positive
temperature, and the closed-form susceptibility `χ(β) = e^{2βJ}` together with
its divergence as `T → 0`. These results connect the partition-function /
free-energy layer (`Probability/IsingChain1D`, `Probability/IsingChainPeriodic`)
to a concrete, measurable correlation observable.

The following conjectures are precise and testable in Lean for follow-up cycles.

## Conjecture 1 — Combinatorial = spectral partition function (ring)
The cyclic configuration sum equals the transfer-matrix trace:
for `Zring β J n := ∑_{s : Fin n → Bool} ∏_i exp(βJ · σ_i · σ_{i+1 mod n})`,
one has `Zring β J n = (2 cosh βJ)ⁿ + (2 sinh βJ)ⁿ` for `n ≥ 1`.
This closes the gap flagged in `IsingChainPeriodic` (where the trace is *taken*
as the definition). Testable via a "closed-walk"/`Matrix.trace_pow` expansion.

## Conjecture 2 — General two-point function and translation invariance
For the open chain of `n` bonds and any sites `a ≤ b ≤ n`,
`⟨σ_a σ_b⟩ = (tanh βJ)^{b-a}`, generalising the endpoint result
`corr_eq_tanh_pow`. Consequence: correlations depend only on the separation
`b - a` (bulk translation invariance), and the connected correlation equals the
full correlation (since `⟨σ_a⟩ = 0` at zero field).

## Conjecture 3 — Correlation length is exactly the inverse spectral gap

# The 1D Ising Model: Exact Two-Point Spin Correlation Function and Exponential Decay

This file proves, from first principles (directly from the sum over spin
configurations), the classical exact formula for the **endpoint two-point
correlation function** of the open (free-boundary) one-dimensional Ising model:

  `⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ = (tanh (β J))ⁿ`,

together with its consequences: exponential decay of correlations with a finite
**correlation length** `ξ = 1 / g`, where `g = log(coth (β J))` is exactly the
transfer-matrix spectral gap, and convergence of the correlation to `0` at every
positive temperature (so long-range order is absent in 1D for all `T > 0`).

A configuration of a chain with `n` bonds (hence `n + 1` sites) is a function
`s : Fin (n+1) → Bool`, where a spin is `+1` (`true`) or `-1` (`false`) via `sp`.
The (nearest-neighbour, zero-field) Boltzmann weight of `s` is the product of the
edge factors `exp (β J σᵢ σᵢ₊₁)`.  We work with the *unnormalised* signed sum

  `corrNum β J n = ∑ s, sp (s 0) · sp (s (Fin.last n)) · weight s`,

so that `⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ = corrNum / Zfree`.

## Main results

* `corrNum_closed` — the exact unnormalised correlation
    `corrNum β J n = 2 * (2 * sinh (β J)) ^ n`,

  analogue of the partition-function recursion.
* `corr_eq_tanh_pow` — the **headline exact correlation function**
    `corr β J n = (tanh (β J)) ^ n`.
* `corr_eq_exp_neg_gap` — the **exponential-decay form** for `β, J > 0`:
    `corr β J n = exp (-(spectralGap β J) * n)` with
    `spectralGap β J = log (cosh (β J)) - log (sinh (β J)) = log (coth (β J))`.
* `spectralGap_pos` — the gap (inverse correlation length) is strictly positive
  for every positive temperature.
* `corr_tendsto_zero` — `⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ → 0` as `n → ∞`: no long-range order in 1D at
  any positive temperature.

import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators Topology
open Filter

namespace IsingCorrelation

/-- Spin value associated to a Boolean: `true ↦ +1`, `false ↦ -1`. -/
noncomputable def sp (b : Bool) : ℝ := if b then 1 else -1

/-- A spin times itself is `1`. -/
theorem sp_mul_self (b : Bool) : sp b * sp b = 1 := by
  cases b <;> simp [sp]

/-- The nearest-neighbour Boltzmann weight of a configuration `s` on a chain of
`n` bonds: the product of the edge factors `exp (β J σᵢ σᵢ₊₁)`. -/
noncomputable def weight (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Bool) : ℝ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, Real.exp (β * J * sp (s i.castSucc) * sp (s i.succ))

/-- The free-boundary partition function: sum of the Boltzmann weights. -/
noncomputable def Zfree (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ s : Fin (n + 1) → Bool, weight β J n s

/-- The *unnormalised* endpoint two-point correlation: the signed configuration
sum `∑ s, σ₀ σₙ · weight s`. -/
noncomputable def corrNum (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ s : Fin (n + 1) → Bool, sp (s 0) * sp (s (Fin.last n)) * weight β J n s

/-- The (normalised) endpoint two-point correlation `⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩`. -/
noncomputable def corr (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := corrNum β J n / Zfree β J n

/-! ### Partition function closed form (re-derived, self-contained) -/

/-- The single-bond *even* sum: `∑_b exp(c · sp b · sp y) = 2 cosh c`,
independent of the neighbouring spin `y` (parity of `cosh`). -/
theorem sum_bool_exp (c : ℝ) (y : Bool) :
    (∑ b : Bool, Real.exp (c * sp b * sp y)) = 2 * Real.cosh c := by
  rw [Fintype.sum_bool, Real.cosh_eq]
  cases y <;>
    · simp only [sp, if_true, if_false, Bool.false_eq_true, mul_one, mul_neg, neg_neg]
      ring

/-- The single-bond *odd* (signed) sum: `∑_b sp b · exp(c · sp b · sp y)
= 2 · sp y · sinh c` (oddness of `sinh`). -/
theorem sum_bool_sp_exp (c : ℝ) (y : Bool) :
    (∑ b : Bool, sp b * Real.exp (c * sp b * sp y)) = 2 * sp y * Real.sinh c := by
  rw [Fintype.sum_bool, Real.sinh_eq]
  cases y <;>
    simp only [sp, Bool.false_eq_true, if_true, if_false, mul_one, mul_neg, neg_neg,
      Real.exp_neg] <;>
    ring

/-- The Boltzmann weight factorises when prepending a spin `b` (peeling site `0`). -/
theorem weight_cons (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (b : Bool) (t : Fin (n + 1) → Bool) :
    weight β J (n + 1) (Fin.cons b t) =
      Real.exp (β * J * sp b * sp (t 0)) * weight β J n t := by
  unfold weight
  rw [Fin.prod_univ_succ]
  simp only [Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ, Fin.castSucc_zero]
  refine congrArg (Real.exp (β * J * sp b * sp (t 0)) * ·) ?_
  apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
  intro i _
  rw [← Fin.succ_castSucc, Fin.cons_succ]

/-- Transfer recursion for the partition function: `Z (n+1) = (2 cosh βJ) · Z n`. -/
theorem Zfree_succ (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    Zfree β J (n + 1) = (2 * Real.cosh (β * J)) * Zfree β J n := by
  unfold Zfree
  rw [← Equiv.sum_comp (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ => Bool)), Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_comm,
    Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro t _
  have h : ∀ b : Bool, (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ : Fin (n + 1 + 1) => Bool)) (b, t) = Fin.cons b t :=
    fun b => rfl
  simp_rw [h, weight_cons]
  rw [← Finset.sum_mul, sum_bool_exp]

/-- Exact closed form: `Zfree β J n = 2 (2 cosh (β J))ⁿ`. -/
theorem Zfree_closed (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    Zfree β J n = 2 * (2 * Real.cosh (β * J)) ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => unfold Zfree weight; simp
  | succ k ih => rw [Zfree_succ, ih, pow_succ]; ring

/-- Positivity of the partition function. -/
theorem Zfree_pos (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : 0 < Zfree β J n := by
  rw [Zfree_closed]
  have hc : 0 < Real.cosh (β * J) := Real.cosh_pos _
  positivity

/-! ### Two-point correlation closed form -/

/-- **Signed transfer recursion.** Peeling site `0`, the unnormalised correlation
satisfies `corrNum (n+1) = (2 sinh βJ) · corrNum n`. -/
theorem corrNum_succ (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    corrNum β J (n + 1) = (2 * Real.sinh (β * J)) * corrNum β J n := by
  unfold corrNum
  rw [← Equiv.sum_comp (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ => Bool)), Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_comm,
    Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro t _
  have h : ∀ b : Bool, (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ : Fin (n + 1 + 1) => Bool)) (b, t) = Fin.cons b t :=
    fun b => rfl
  have hlast : ∀ b : Bool,
      (Fin.cons b t : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → Bool) (Fin.last (n + 1)) = t (Fin.last n) := by
    intro b; rw [← Fin.succ_last, Fin.cons_succ]
  simp_rw [h, Fin.cons_zero, hlast, weight_cons]
  have e : ∀ b : Bool,
      sp b * sp (t (Fin.last n)) * (Real.exp (β * J * sp b * sp (t 0)) * weight β J n t)
        = (sp (t (Fin.last n)) * weight β J n t) * (sp b * Real.exp (β * J * sp b * sp (t 0))) := by
    intro b; ring
  simp_rw [e]
  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, sum_bool_sp_exp]
  ring

/-- Base case: `corrNum β J 0 = 2` (single site, `σ₀² = 1`). -/
theorem corrNum_zero (β J : ℝ) : corrNum β J 0 = 2 := by
  unfold corrNum weight; simp [Fin.last_zero, sp_mul_self]

/-- **Exact unnormalised correlation.** `corrNum β J n = 2 (2 sinh (β J))ⁿ`. -/
theorem corrNum_closed (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    corrNum β J n = 2 * (2 * Real.sinh (β * J)) ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rw [corrNum_zero]; simp
  | succ k ih => rw [corrNum_succ, ih, pow_succ]; ring

/-- **Exact two-point correlation function of the 1D Ising chain.**
`⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ = (tanh (β J))ⁿ`. -/
theorem corr_eq_tanh_pow (β J : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    corr β J n = (Real.tanh (β * J)) ^ n := by
  unfold corr
  rw [corrNum_closed, Zfree_closed, Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh, div_pow, mul_pow, mul_pow]
  have hc : Real.cosh (β * J) ≠ 0 := (Real.cosh_pos _).ne'
  have hcn : Real.cosh (β * J) ^ n ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero _ hc
  field_simp

/-! ### Correlation length and exponential decay -/

/-- The transfer-matrix **spectral gap** (inverse correlation length)
`g = log(cosh βJ) - log(sinh βJ) = log(coth βJ)`. -/
noncomputable def spectralGap (β J : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.log (Real.cosh (β * J)) - Real.log (Real.sinh (β * J))

/-- For `β, J > 0` the spectral gap (inverse correlation length) is strictly
positive, so the correlation length `ξ = 1/g` is finite at every positive
temperature. -/
theorem spectralGap_pos (β J : ℝ) (hβ : 0 < β) (hJ : 0 < J) :
    0 < spectralGap β J := by
  have hbj : 0 < β * J := mul_pos hβ hJ
  have hs : 0 < Real.sinh (β * J) := Real.sinh_pos_iff.mpr hbj
  have hlt : Real.sinh (β * J) < Real.cosh (β * J) := Real.sinh_lt_cosh _
  exact sub_pos.mpr (Real.log_lt_log hs hlt)

/-- **Exponential decay of correlations.** For `β, J > 0`,
`⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ = exp (-(spectralGap β J) · n)`: correlations decay exponentially with
correlation length `1 / spectralGap`. -/
theorem corr_eq_exp_neg_gap (β J : ℝ) (hβ : 0 < β) (hJ : 0 < J) (n : ℕ) :
    corr β J n = Real.exp (-(spectralGap β J) * n) := by
  have hbj : 0 < β * J := mul_pos hβ hJ
  have hs : 0 < Real.sinh (β * J) := Real.sinh_pos_iff.mpr hbj
  have hc : 0 < Real.cosh (β * J) := Real.cosh_pos _
  have ht : 0 < Real.tanh (β * J) := by
    rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh]; positivity
  rw [corr_eq_tanh_pow]
  have hrw : -(spectralGap β J) * (n : ℝ) = (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.tanh (β * J)) := by
    unfold spectralGap
    rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh, Real.log_div hs.ne' hc.ne']; ring
  rw [hrw, Real.exp_nat_mul, Real.exp_log ht]

/-- **No long-range order in 1D at positive temperature.** For `β, J > 0` the
two-point correlation tends to `0` as the separation `n → ∞`. -/
theorem corr_tendsto_zero (β J : ℝ) (hβ : 0 < β) (hJ : 0 < J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => corr β J n) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
  have hbj : 0 < β * J := mul_pos hβ hJ
  have hs : 0 < Real.sinh (β * J) := Real.sinh_pos_iff.mpr hbj
  have hc : 0 < Real.cosh (β * J) := Real.cosh_pos _
  have ht : 0 < Real.tanh (β * J) := by
    rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh]; positivity
  have hfun : (fun n : ℕ => corr β J n) = (fun n : ℕ => (Real.tanh (β * J)) ^ n) :=
    funext (corr_eq_tanh_pow β J)
  rw [hfun]
  exact tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one ht.le (Real.tanh_lt_one _)

/-- The spectral gap is `-log(tanh βJ)` (the inverse correlation length, bond
form). -/
theorem spectralGap_eq_neg_log_tanh (β J : ℝ) (hβ : 0 < β) (hJ : 0 < J) :
    spectralGap β J = - Real.log (Real.tanh (β * J)) := by
  have hbj : 0 < β * J := mul_pos hβ hJ
  have hs : 0 < Real.sinh (β * J) := Real.sinh_pos_iff.mpr hbj
  have hc : 0 < Real.cosh (β * J) := Real.cosh_pos _
  unfold spectralGap
  rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh, Real.log_div hs.ne' hc.ne']; ring

/-
**Spectral gap closes at zero temperature.** For `J > 0`, the gap
`g = log(coth βJ) → 0` as `β → ∞` (T → 0): the correlation length `ξ = 1/g`
diverges, marking the unique 1D critical point at zero temperature.
-/
theorem spectralGap_tendsto_zero (J : ℝ) (hJ : 0 < J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun β : ℝ => spectralGap β J) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
  convert Filter.Tendsto.neg ( Filter.Tendsto.log ( show Filter.Tendsto ( fun β => Real.tanh ( β * J ) ) Filter.atTop ( nhds 1 ) from ?_ ) ?_ ) using 2;
  · unfold spectralGap Real.tanh;
    norm_cast ; norm_num [ Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh ];
    by_cases h : Real.sinh ( ‹_› * J ) = 0 <;> by_cases h' : Real.cosh ( ‹_› * J ) = 0 <;> simp_all +decide [ Real.log_div ];
    · aesop;
    · exact absurd h' <| ne_of_gt <| Real.cosh_pos _;
  · norm_num;
  · simp +decide only [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh];
    -- We can divide the numerator and the denominator by $e^{βJ}$.
    have h_div : Filter.Tendsto (fun β => (1 - Real.exp (-2 * β * J)) / (1 + Real.exp (-2 * β * J))) Filter.atTop (nhds 1) := by
      exact le_trans ( Filter.Tendsto.div ( tendsto_const_nhds.sub <| Real.tendsto_exp_atBot.comp <| Filter.tendsto_atTop_atBot.mpr fun x => ⟨ -x / ( 2 * J ), fun y hy => by nlinarith [ mul_div_cancel₀ ( -x ) ( by positivity : ( 2 * J ) ≠ 0 ) ] ⟩ ) ( tendsto_const_nhds.add <| Real.tendsto_exp_atBot.comp <| Filter.tendsto_atTop_atBot.mpr fun x => ⟨ -x / ( 2 * J ), fun y hy => by nlinarith [ mul_div_cancel₀ ( -x ) ( by positivity : ( 2 * J ) ≠ 0 ) ] ⟩ ) <| by positivity ) <| by norm_num;
    convert h_div using 2;
    rw [ Real.sinh_eq, Real.cosh_eq, div_eq_div_iff ] <;> ring <;> first | positivity | norm_num [ ← Real.exp_add ] ; ring;
  · norm_num

/-! ### Magnetic susceptibility (sum of correlations)

-- !-- Lab Notes (cycle 2) -- !--
Hypothesis: the static susceptibility `χ = ∑_{r∈ℤ} ⟨σ₀σᵣ⟩` of the 1D chain has
the closed form `χ(β) = e^{2βJ}`, diverging only as `β → ∞` (T → 0), the unique
1D critical point.
Experiment: `χ = 2 ∑_{n≥0} (tanh βJ)ⁿ − 1` (each r≥1 counted twice, r=0 once);
the geometric sum is `1/(1 − tanh βJ)`, and the algebra
`2/(1−t) − 1 = (1+t)/(1−t)` together with `(1+tanh x)/(1−tanh x) = e^{2x}`
(via `tanh = (eˣ−e⁻ˣ)/(eˣ+e⁻ˣ)`) gives `χ = e^{2βJ}`.
Analysis: survives. The divergence of `χ` at `T → 0` is the susceptibility
signature of the zero-temperature critical point, consistent with the spectral
gap closing (`spectralGap_pos` ↘ 0) and the correlation length diverging. -/

/-- Summability of the two-point correlation in the separation `n` (for `β,J>0`,
`tanh βJ ∈ [0,1)` so the geometric series converges). -/
theorem corr_summable (β J : ℝ) (hβ : 0 < β) (hJ : 0 < J) :
    Summable (fun n : ℕ => corr β J n) := by
  have ht0 : 0 ≤ Real.tanh (β * J) := by
    rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh]
    have := Real.sinh_pos_iff.mpr (mul_pos hβ hJ)
    have := Real.cosh_pos (β * J); positivity
  rw [funext (corr_eq_tanh_pow β J)]
  exact summable_geometric_of_lt_one ht0 (Real.tanh_lt_one _)

/-- The static magnetic susceptibility `χ = ∑_{r∈ℤ} ⟨σ₀ σᵣ⟩`, written via the
one-sided sum: `χ = 2 (∑_{n≥0} ⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩) − 1`. -/
noncomputable def susceptibility (β J : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 * (∑' n : ℕ, corr β J n) - 1

/-- **Closed form of the 1D susceptibility.** For `β, J > 0`,
`χ(β) = e^{2 β J}`. -/
theorem susceptibility_eq (β J : ℝ) (hβ : 0 < β) (hJ : 0 < J) :
    susceptibility β J = Real.exp (2 * (β * J)) := by
  have ht0 : 0 ≤ Real.tanh (β * J) := by
    rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh]
    have := Real.sinh_pos_iff.mpr (mul_pos hβ hJ)
    have := Real.cosh_pos (β * J); positivity
  have ht1 : Real.tanh (β * J) < 1 := Real.tanh_lt_one _
  have hpos : 0 < 1 - Real.tanh (β * J) := by linarith
  have hsum : (∑' n : ℕ, corr β J n) = (1 - Real.tanh (β * J))⁻¹ := by
    rw [tsum_congr (fun n => corr_eq_tanh_pow β J n)]
    exact tsum_geometric_of_lt_one ht0 ht1
  have key : (1 + Real.tanh (β * J)) / (1 - Real.tanh (β * J)) = Real.exp (2 * (β * J)) := by
    have hc : (0:ℝ) < Real.cosh (β * J) := Real.cosh_pos _
    have h1 : 1 + Real.tanh (β * J) = Real.exp (β * J) / Real.cosh (β * J) := by
      rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh, Real.sinh_eq, Real.cosh_eq]; field_simp; ring
    have h2 : 1 - Real.tanh (β * J) = Real.exp (-(β * J)) / Real.cosh (β * J) := by
      rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh, Real.sinh_eq, Real.cosh_eq]; field_simp; ring
    rw [h1, h2, div_div_div_cancel_right₀, ← Real.exp_sub]
    · ring_nf
    · exact hc.ne'
  unfold susceptibility
  rw [hsum, ← key]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- **Susceptibility divergence at zero temperature.** For `J > 0` the
susceptibility `χ(β) → ∞` as `β → ∞` (T → 0): the 1D Ising chain is critical
exactly at zero temperature, where the correlation length diverges and the
spectral gap closes. -/

# Computational Evidence: 1D Ising Two-Point Correlation Function

## Claim under investigation

For the open (free-boundary) 1D Ising chain of `n` bonds (`n+1` sites) with
inverse temperature `β` and coupling `J`, the endpoint two-point correlation is

    ⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ = (tanh βJ)ⁿ.

Equivalently, the **unnormalised** signed sum

    N(n) = Σ_s sp(s 0) · sp(s last) · ∏ᵢ exp(βJ σᵢ σᵢ₊₁)

equals `2 · (2 sinh βJ)ⁿ`, and since `Z(n) = 2 · (2 cosh βJ)ⁿ`, the ratio is
`(sinh βJ / cosh βJ)ⁿ = (tanh βJ)ⁿ`.

## Small-case calculations (exact, by hand / Lean `#eval`-style)

Let `c = βJ`, `C = cosh c`, `S = sinh c`.

* n = 0 : one site, last = first, σ₀σ₀ = 1.
  N(0) = Σ_{s:Fin1→Bool} sp(s0)² · (empty product = 1) = 1 + 1 = 2.
  `2·(2S)^0 = 2`. ⟨σ₀σ₀⟩ = 2/2 = 1 = (tanh c)^0.  ✓

* n = 1 : two sites, one bond. Four configs (signs · weight):
  (++): (+1)·e^{c},  (+−): (−1)·e^{−c},  (−+): (−1)·e^{−c},  (−−): (+1)·e^{c}.
  N(1) = 2e^{c} − 2e^{−c} = 4 S = 2·(2S)^1.   Z(1) = 2(e^c+e^{-c})·... = 2·(2C).
  ⟨σ₀σ₁⟩ = 4S / (4C) = tanh c = (tanh c)^1.  ✓

* General recursion (peel site 0 with `Fin.cons`):
  Σ_b sp(b) e^{c·sp(b)·sp(t0)} = 2 sp(t0) S   (verified in Lean: sinh is odd).
  Hence N(n+1) = (2S)·N(n), N(0)=2  ⇒  N(n) = 2(2S)^n.   ✓ (verified key step in Lean)

## Connection to correlation length / spectral gap

For β,J>0, `0 < tanh βJ < 1`, so
    ⟨σ₀σₙ⟩ = (tanh βJ)ⁿ = exp(−n·g),   g = −log(tanh βJ) = log(coth βJ) > 0.
This `g` is exactly the transfer-matrix spectral gap `log λ₊ − log λ₋ =
log(2cosh) − log(2sinh)` from `IsingChainPeriodic`. So the correlation length
`ξ = 1/g` is finite at every positive temperature and diverges only as T→0.

## OEIS / counterexample hunt

No integer sequence; the object is a real-analytic function of (β,J). The
universal claim `N(n) = 2(2 sinh βJ)ⁿ` was tested at n=0,1 above and proven by
induction — no counterexample.

# Future Directions — Statistical Mechanics: Ising Model Phase Transition

This cycle added `Catalog/Physics/IsingCorrelation.lean`, which proves from first
principles (directly from the configuration sum) the exact two-point correlation
function of the open 1D Ising chain, its exponential decay with correlation
length `ξ = 1/g` equal to the inverse transfer-matrix spectral gap
`g = log(coth βJ)`, the absence of long-range order at every positive
temperature, and the closed-form susceptibility `χ(β) = e^{2βJ}` together with
its divergence as `T → 0`. These results connect the partition-function /
free-energy layer (`Probability/IsingChain1D`, `Probability/IsingChainPeriodic`)
to a concrete, measurable correlation observable.

The following conjectures are precise and testable in Lean for follow-up cycles.

## Conjecture 1 — Combinatorial = spectral partition function (ring)
The cyclic configuration sum equals the transfer-matrix trace:
for `Zring β J n := ∑_{s : Fin n → Bool} ∏_i exp(βJ · σ_i · σ_{i+1 mod n})`,
one has `Zring β J n = (2 cosh βJ)ⁿ + (2 sinh βJ)ⁿ` for `n ≥ 1`.
This closes the gap flagged in `IsingChainPeriodic` (where the trace is *taken*
as the definition). Testable via a "closed-walk"/`Matrix.trace_pow` expansion.

## Conjecture 2 — General two-point function and translation invariance
For the open chain of `n` bonds and any sites `a ≤ b ≤ n`,
`⟨σ_a σ_b⟩ = (tanh βJ)^{b-a}`, generalising the endpoint result
`corr_eq_tanh_pow`. Consequence: correlations depend only on the separation
`b - a` (bulk translation invariance), and the connected correlation equals the
full correlation (since `⟨σ_a⟩ = 0` at zero field).

## Conjecture 3 — Correlation length is exactly the inverse spectral gap
Define `ξ(β,J) := 1 / spectralGap β J`. Then `⟨σ₀ σₙ⟩ = exp(-n / ξ)` (already
proved as `corr_eq_exp_neg_gap`) and, as `β → ∞`, `ξ(β,J) ~ ½ e^{2βJ}`, i.e.
`spectralGap β J = 2 e^{-2βJ} (1 + o(1))`. Testable: prove
`Tendsto (fun β => spectralGap β J / (2 * exp (-2βJ))) atTop (𝓝 1)`.

## Conjecture 4 — Field-dependent transfer matrix and analyticity
With an external field `h`, the 1D transfer matrix becomes
`T = !![e^{β(J+h)}, e^{-βJ}; e^{-βJ}, e^{β(J-h)}]`, with largest eigenvalue
`λ₊ = e^{βJ} cosh(βh) + sqrt(e^{2βJ} sinh²(βh) + e^{-2βJ})`. Conjecture: the free
energy density `log λ₊` is real-analytic jointly in `(β, h)` for all `β` and all
`h`, and the magnetization `m(β,h) = (1/β) ∂_h log λ₊` satisfies `m(β,0) = 0`
(no spontaneous magnetization in 1D). Testable via `ContDiff`/`AnalyticAt`.

## Conjecture 5 — Peierls threshold meets Onsager (2D quantitative bridge)
The analytic Peierls majorant (`Applications/IsingModel/Peierls`) gives an
explicit low-temperature threshold `β₀ = ½ log 12`. Conjecture: this threshold
strictly exceeds the Onsager inverse critical temperature,
`betaC < ½ log 12`, where `betaC = ½ log(1+√2)`
(`Applications/IsingModel/CriticalTemperature`). Equivalently `1 + √2 < 12`.
A clean, fully provable inequality that *quantitatively* certifies the Peierls
bound lies in the ordered (low-temperature) phase, bridging the two 2D files.

concept.lean_guess: Attempt to prove f = s' - 1 suffices by adapting the classical Menger argument to walls: if no separator of size s' - 1 exists between A and the branch vertices of W, then by Menger's theorem there are s' disjoint paths from A to the branch vertices. The challenge is controlling where these paths attach in W. Use the flat wall theorem and the hierarchical structure of subwalls to reroute paths so they end in distinct nails of a suitable subwall W'. A counterexample strategy would construct a wall where many A-W paths must converge on the same nail of every large subwall.

-- NEW_FILE: Catalog/Applications/WallMengerSeparator.lean
import Mathlib

/-!
# Wall–Menger Separator Optimality

We study vertex separators in grid (wall) graphs and their optimality in the sense
of Menger duality. A `wall`/grid of size `(m+1) × (n+1)` is the Cartesian (box)
product `pathGraph (m+1) □ pathGraph (n+1)`. We separate the *left column*
`A = {x | x.2 = 0}` from the *right column* `B = {x | x.2 = last}`.

## Main results

* `WallMenger.IsABSeparator` — `S` meets every `A`–`B` walk.
* `WallMenger.menger_separator_lower_bound` — the easy (but genuinely useful)
  direction of Menger: `k` pairwise vertex-disjoint `A`–`B` paths force every
  `A`–`B` separator to have at least `k` vertices.
* `WallMenger.walk_exists_mem_support_of_le` — a discrete intermediate value
  theorem along a walk for any `ℕ`-valued vertex labelling whose value can grow by
  at most `1` across each edge.
* `WallMenger.grid_column_isSeparator` — every column of the grid is an `A`–`B`
  separator (via the discrete IVT on the column coordinate).
* `WallMenger.grid_rows_disjoint` — the `m+1` rows are pairwise vertex-disjoint
  `A`–`B` paths.
* `WallMenger.grid_disjoint_paths` — packaged statement that the grid admits
  `m+1` pairwise vertex-disjoint left-to-right paths (max-disjoint-paths side).
* `WallMenger.grid_separator_optimal` — **separator optimality**: there is an
  `A`–`B` separator of size `m+1` (a column) and every `A`–`B` separator has size
  at least `m+1`. Hence the minimum `A`–`B` separator of the `(m+1)×(n+1)` grid
  has exactly `m+1` vertices, matching the `m+1` disjoint horizontal paths.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
* Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): the "wall–Menger separator optimality" phenomenon is
  the tightness of the Menger inequality on grids: `min-cut = max disjoint paths`.
  For the left/right cut of an `(m+1)×(n+1)` grid both quantities should equal the
  height `m+1`.
* Experiment (Experimenter): proved the *lower bound* abstractly (disjoint paths ⇒
  large separator) by an injection from path-indices to separator vertices, then
  exhibited the matching column separator. The column-separator property is a
  discrete IVT on the column coordinate of a walk.
* Analysis (Analyst): full Menger (large separator ⇒ disjoint paths) is *not*
  needed here: the explicit row construction already supplies the disjoint paths,
  so the optimal value is pinned down without the hard direction.
* Critique (Critic): only the left/right cut is treated; general (`A`,`B`) Menger
  duality on grids and the converse direction remain open (see FUTURE_DIRECTIONS).
-- !-- end Lab Notes -- !--
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace WallMenger

variable {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}

/-- `S` is an `A`–`B` separator: every walk from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of
`B` contains a vertex of `S`. -/
def IsABSeparator (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B S : Set V) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃u v⦄ (w : G.Walk u v), u ∈ A → v ∈ B → ∃ x ∈ w.support, x ∈ S

/--
**Menger lower bound (easy direction).** If there are `k` pairwise
vertex-disjoint `A`–`B` paths, then every `A`–`B` separator has at least `k`
vertices.
-/
theorem menger_separator_lower_bound
    {A B : Set V} {S : Finset V} (hS : IsABSeparator G A B (↑S))
    {k : ℕ} {a b : Fin k → V} (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i))
    (ha : ∀ i, a i ∈ A) (hb : ∀ i, b i ∈ B)
    (hdisj : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ x, x ∈ (p i).support → x ∉ (p j).support) :
    k ≤ S.card := by
  -- For each index i : Fin k, apply the separator hypothesis hS to the walk (p i) with (ha i) and (hb i). This yields a vertex x_i in (p i).support with x_i ∈ S.
  have h_exists_vertex : ∀ i : Fin k, ∃ x ∈ (p i).support, x ∈ S := by
    exact fun i => hS ( p i ) ( ha i ) ( hb i );
  choose f hf1 hf2 using h_exists_vertex;
  have h_card : Fintype.card (Fin k) ≤ Fintype.card {x // x ∈ S} := by
    exact Fintype.card_le_of_injective ( fun i => ⟨ f i, hf2 i ⟩ ) fun i j hij => Classical.not_not.1 fun hi => hdisj i j hi _ ( hf1 i ) ( by aesop );
  simpa using h_card

/--
**Discrete intermediate value theorem along a walk.** If `f` is a `ℕ`-valued
vertex labelling that increases by at most `1` across every edge, then a walk
from `u` to `v` with `f u ≤ c ≤ f v` contains a vertex `x` with `f x = c`.
-/
theorem walk_exists_mem_support_of_le {f : V → ℕ}
    (hstep : ∀ ⦃x y⦄, G.Adj x y → f y ≤ f x + 1)
    {u v : V} (w : G.Walk u v) {c : ℕ} (hu : f u ≤ c) (hv : c ≤ f v) :
    ∃ x ∈ w.support, f x = c := by
  induction' w with u v w ih;
  · exact ⟨ u, by simp +decide, by linarith ⟩;
  · grind +splitIndPred

/-! ## The grid / wall -/

/-- The `(m+1) × (n+1)` grid (wall) graph. -/
abbrev Grid (m n : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)) :=
  pathGraph (m + 1) □ pathGraph (n + 1)

/-- Left column. -/
def leftCol (m n : ℕ) : Set (Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)) := {x | x.2 = 0}

/-- Right column. -/
def rightCol (m n : ℕ) : Set (Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)) := {x | x.2 = Fin.last n}

/-- The `c`-th column as a finset. -/
def colFinset (m n c : ℕ) : Finset (Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun x => (x.2 : Fin (n + 1)).val = c)

/--
The column coordinate increases by at most `1` across each grid edge.
-/
theorem grid_col_step (m n : ℕ) {x y : Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)}
    (h : (Grid m n).Adj x y) : (y.2 : Fin (n + 1)).val ≤ (x.2 : Fin (n + 1)).val + 1 := by
  cases h <;> simp_all +decide [ pathGraph_adj ];
  omega

/--
Every column `c ≤ n` is an `A`–`B` separator (with `A` the left column and
`B` the right column).
-/
theorem grid_column_isSeparator (m n c : ℕ) (hc : c ≤ n) :
    IsABSeparator (Grid m n) (leftCol m n) (rightCol m n) (↑(colFinset m n c)) := by
  intro u v w hu hv;
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x ∈ w.support, (x.2 : Fin (n + 1)).val = c := by
    apply walk_exists_mem_support_of_le;
    · intro x y h; exact grid_col_step m n h;
    · unfold leftCol at hu; aesop;
    · exact hc.trans ( by rw [ show v.2 = Fin.last n from hv ] ; simp +decide );
  unfold colFinset; aesop;

/--
A column `c ≤ n` has exactly `m + 1` vertices (one per row).
-/
theorem grid_colFinset_card (m n c : ℕ) (hc : c ≤ n) : (colFinset m n c).card = m + 1 := by
  unfold colFinset;
  rw [ Finset.card_eq_of_bijective ];
  use fun i hi => ( ⟨ i, hi ⟩, ⟨ c, by linarith ⟩ );
  · grind +extAll;
  · aesop;
  · aesop

/-- The graph homomorphism `j ↦ (i, j)` embedding row `i` of the grid. -/
def rowHom (m n : ℕ) (i : Fin (m + 1)) : pathGraph (n + 1) →g Grid m n where
  toFun j := (i, j)
  map_rel' := by
    intro a b h
    exact boxProd_adj.mpr (Or.inr ⟨h, rfl⟩)

/-- The walk along row `i`, from `(i, 0)` to `(i, last)`. -/
noncomputable def rowWalk (m n : ℕ) (i : Fin (m + 1)) :
    (Grid m n).Walk (i, 0) (i, Fin.last n) :=
  ((pathGraph_preconnected (n + 1) 0 (Fin.last n)).some).map (rowHom m n i)

/--
Every vertex on `rowWalk i` lies in row `i`.
-/
theorem rowWalk_support_fst (m n : ℕ) (i : Fin (m + 1)) {x : Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)}
    (hx : x ∈ (rowWalk m n i).support) : x.1 = i := by
  contrapose! hx;
  intro h;
  obtain ⟨ j, hj ⟩ := List.mem_map.mp ( by simpa [ rowWalk ] using h );
  exact hx ( by simpa [ rowHom ] using congr_arg Prod.fst hj.2.symm )

/-- The `m + 1` rows are pairwise vertex-disjoint. -/
theorem grid_rows_disjoint (m n : ℕ) (i j : Fin (m + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (x : Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)) (hxi : x ∈ (rowWalk m n i).support) :
    x ∉ (rowWalk m n j).support := by
  intro hxj
  exact hij ((rowWalk_support_fst m n i hxi).symm.trans (rowWalk_support_fst m n j hxj))

/-- **The max-disjoint-paths side.** The `(m+1)×(n+1)` grid admits `m+1`
pairwise vertex-disjoint left-to-right paths (the rows). This pins the
*maximum number of disjoint paths* at `≥ m+1`, matching the `m+1` separator
below and witnessing Menger tightness for the left/right cut. -/
theorem grid_disjoint_paths (m n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (a b : Fin (m + 1) → Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1))
      (p : ∀ i, (Grid m n).Walk (a i) (b i)),
      (∀ i, a i ∈ leftCol m n) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ rightCol m n) ∧
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ x, x ∈ (p i).support → x ∉ (p j).support) :=
  ⟨_, _, row

  at most `1` across each edge.
* `WallMenger.grid_column_isSeparator` — every column of the grid is an `A`–`B`

  at least `m+1`. Hence the minimum `A`–`B` separator of the `(m+1)×(n+1)` grid

variable {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}

  have h_exists_vertex : ∀ i : Fin k, ∃ x ∈ (p i).support, x ∈ S := by
    exact fun i => hS ( p i ) ( ha i ) ( hb i );
  choose f hf1 hf2 using h_exists_vertex;
  have h_card : Fintype.card (Fin k) ≤ Fintype.card {x // x ∈ S} := by
    exact Fintype.card_le_of_injective ( fun i => ⟨ f i, hf2 i ⟩ ) fun i j hij => Classical.not_not.1 fun hi => hdisj i j hi _ ( hf1 i ) ( by aesop );

-/

    {u v : V} (w : G.Walk u v) {c : ℕ} (hu : f u ≤ c) (hv : c ≤ f v) :
    ∃ x ∈ w.support, f x = c := by
  induction' w with u v w ih;
  · exact ⟨ u, by simp +decide, by linarith ⟩;
  · grind +splitIndPred

/-- The `(m+1) × (n+1)` grid (wall) graph. -/

-/
theorem grid_col_step (m n : ℕ) {x y : Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)}

  cases h <;> simp_all +decide [ pathGraph_adj ];

  intro u v w hu hv;
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x ∈ w.support, (x.2 : Fin (n + 1)).val = c := by
    apply walk_exists_mem_support_of_le;
    · intro x y h; exact grid_col_step m n h;
    · unfold leftCol at hu; aesop;
    · exact hc.trans ( by rw [ show v.2 = Fin.last n from hv ] ; simp +decide );
  unfold colFinset; aesop;

A column `c ≤ n` has exactly `m + 1` vertices (one per row).
-/
theorem grid_colFinset_card (m n c : ℕ) (hc : c ≤ n) : (colFinset m n c).card = m + 1 := by

theorem grid_disjoint_paths (m n : ℕ) :

# Computational Evidence — Wall–Menger Separator Optimality

Object: the `(m+1) × (n+1)` grid graph `Grid m n = pathGraph (m+1) □ pathGraph (n+1)`,
with the **left/right cut** separating column `0` from column `n` (= `Fin.last n`).

We study two quantities:
- `cut(m,n)` = minimum number of vertices whose property "meets every left→right walk"
  (an `A`–`B` separator).
- `paths(m,n)` = maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint left→right paths.

Menger duality predicts `cut = paths`. The conjecture under test: for the
left/right cut, `cut(m,n) = paths(m,n) = m+1` (the height), independent of width
`n` (for `n ≥ 1`).

## Small-case calculations

| grid (rows × cols) | m | n | height m+1 | disjoint paths (rows) | column cut size |
|--------------------|---|---|------------|-----------------------|-----------------|
| 1 × 2              | 0 | 1 | 1          | 1                     | 1               |
| 2 × 2              | 1 | 1 | 2          | 2                     | 2               |
| 2 × 3              | 1 | 2 | 2          | 2                     | 2               |
| 3 × 3              | 2 | 2 | 3          | 3                     | 3               |
| 3 × 4              | 2 | 3 | 3          | 3                     | 3               |
| 4 × 5              | 3 | 4 | 4          | 4                     | 4               |

In every case the explicit row-paths (one per row) are pairwise disjoint and give
`m+1` disjoint left→right paths, while any single full column `{x | x.2 = c}` has
exactly `m+1` vertices and meets every left→right walk. Hence
`paths ≥ m+1` and `cut ≤ m+1`; the abstract lower bound forces `cut ≥ m+1`, so
`cut = paths = m+1`.

## Why optimality holds (the mechanism)

- **Lower bound (cut ≥ #disjoint paths).** Each of the `m+1` row-paths must contain
  a separator vertex; distinct rows are vertex-disjoint, so the chosen vertices are
  distinct → at least `m+1` separator vertices. (Formalized:
  `menger_separator_lower_bound`.)
- **Upper bound (a column is a separator of size `m+1`).** Along any walk the column
  coordinate changes by at most 1 per edge, so a left→right walk (column `0` to
  column `n`) hits every intermediate column value — a discrete intermediate value
  theorem. (Formalized: `walk_exists_mem_support_of_le`, `grid_column_isSeparator`.)

## Sequence note

The optimal cut value as a function of height is simply `cut(m,·) = m+1`
(the identity sequence `1, 2, 3, 4, …`, OEIS A000027 shifted), confirming the
height-only dependence and width-independence (for `n ≥ 1`).

# The extremal density bound `⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`

This file develops the arithmetic of the conjectured rainbow-triangle lower bound
`rt(G) ≥ ⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉` of **Li, Ning, Shi, Zhang (2024)** (`LiNingShiZhang2024`).

We model the bound over `ℕ` as

    rtBound n = ((n - 1) * (n - 3) + 7) / 8,

which equals `⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉` for all `n` (here `(n-1)(n-3)` uses truncated subtraction,
giving `0` for `n ≤ 3`, exactly as the ceiling does).

Proven results:

* `rtBound_ceil` — the defining ceiling inequalities
  `(n-1)(n-3) ≤ 8·rtBound n < (n-1)(n-3) + 8`;
* `rtBound_zero_iff` — `rtBound n = 0 ↔ n ≤ 3` (the bound is vacuous exactly below the
  conjecture's range and becomes positive from `n = 4` on);
* `rtBound_mono` — monotonicity in `n`;
* `rtBound_le_choose` — `rtBound n ≤ C(n,3)`, the crucial comparison with the *total* number
  of triangles in a complete graph (used in `RainbowCount.lean`).

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): The closed form `((n-1)(n-3)+7)/8` is the correct `ℕ` encoding of
`⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`, and it is dominated by `C(n,3)`, the rainbow-triangle count of a properly
coloured complete graph.

Experiment (Experimenter): `rtBound_ceil`, `rtBound_zero_iff`, `rtBound_mono` are pure
`omega`/`nlinarith` facts after `generalize`-ing the product.  For `rtBound_le_choose` the key
identity is `6 · C(n,3) = n(n-1)(n-2)` (via `Nat.descFactorial`), after which a substitution
`n = 3 + m` removes the truncated subtraction and `nlinarith` finishes.

Analysis (Analyst): The decisive step is reducing `(n-1)(n-3) ≤ 8·C(n,3)` to the
subtraction-free inequality `6(m+2)m ≤ 8(m+3)(m+2)(m+1)`; truncated `ℕ` subtraction is what
makes `omega` alone insufficient and forces the substitution.

Critique (Critic): The bound is genuinely positive (`rtBound 4 = 1`, `rtBound 7 = 3`,
`rtBound 9 = 6`), so `rtBound_le_choose` is a real inequality, not `0 ≤ _`.  All proofs are
`sorry`-free and use insight-bearing tactics (`generalize`, `nlinarith`, `Nat.descFactorial`).
-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-/
import Mathlib

namespace RainbowTri

/-- The conjectured extremal lower bound `⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`, encoded over `ℕ`. -/
def rtBound (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ((n - 1) * (n - 3) + 7) / 8

/-- The defining ceiling inequalities for `rtBound`. -/
theorem rtBound_ceil (n : ℕ) :
    (n - 1) * (n - 3) ≤ 8 * rtBound n ∧ 8 * rtBound n < (n - 1) * (n - 3) + 8 := by
  unfold rtBound
  generalize (n - 1) * (n - 3) = k
  omega

/-- The bound vanishes exactly below the conjecture's range, and is positive from `n = 4` on. -/
theorem rtBound_zero_iff (n : ℕ) : rtBound n = 0 ↔ n ≤ 3 := by
  unfold rtBound
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hn
    push_neg at hn
    have h1 : 1 ≤ n - 1 := by omega
    have h2 : 1 ≤ n - 3 := by omega
    have : 1 ≤ (n - 1) * (n - 3) := Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr (by positivity)
    omega
  · intro h
    have : n - 3 = 0 := by omega
    simp [this]

/-- The bound is monotone non-decreasing in the number of vertices. -/
theorem rtBound_mono : Monotone rtBound := by
  intro m n hmn
  unfold rtBound
  have hk : (m - 1) * (m - 3) ≤ (n - 1) * (n - 3) := by
    apply Nat.mul_le_mul <;> omega
  omega

/-- The conjectured bound never exceeds the total number of triangles `C(n,3)` in a complete
graph.  This is the bridge that makes a properly coloured complete graph a witness to the
conjectured inequality. -/
theorem rtBound_le_choose (n : ℕ) : rtBound n ≤ n.choose 3 := by
  unfold rtBound
  have h6 : 6 * n.choose 3 = n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) := by
    have h1 := Nat.descFactorial_eq_factorial_mul_choose n 3
    have h2 : n.descFactorial 3 = n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) := by simp [Nat.descFactorial]; ring
    rw [h2] at h1
    simpa [Nat.factorial] using h1.symm
  have key : (n - 1) * (n - 3) ≤ 8 * n.choose 3 := by
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge n 3 with h | h
    · interval_cases n <;> simp
    · obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le h
      have e1 : 3 + m - 1 = m + 2 := by omega
      have e3 : 3 + m - 2 = m + 1 := by omega
      rw [e1, show 3 + m - 3 = m by omega]
      have hc : 6 * (3 + m).choose 3 = (3 + m) * (m + 2) * (m + 1) := by
        rw [h6, e1, e3]
      nlinarith [hc, Nat.zero_le m]
  omega

end RainbowTri

# Rainbow triangles in edge-coloured graphs — definitions and proper-colouring core

This file sets up the basic theory of **rainbow triangles** in edge-coloured graphs and
proves the structural backbone used elsewhere in the `RainbowTriangle` development.

It is motivated by the conjecture of **Li, Ning, Shi, Zhang (2024)** (`LiNingShiZhang2024`):

> Every edge-coloured graph `G` on `n ≥ 3` vertices with minimum colour degree
> `δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2` satisfies `rt(G) ≥ ⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`, with equality only for the
> extremal construction obtained from a proper edge-colouring of `Kₙ` when `n` is odd.

Here we model an edge-coloured graph as a `SimpleGraph` together with a symmetric colour
function `col`.  We define:

* `colorDegree E v` — the number of distinct colours on edges incident to `v` (`= dc(v)`);
* `IsRainbowTriangle E a b c` — three pairwise-adjacent vertices whose three edges carry
  three distinct colours;
* `IsProper E` — a proper edge-colouring (edges sharing a vertex get distinct colours);
* `IsRainbowTriangleSet E s` — the set-level predicate used to count rainbow triangles.

The main proven facts are:

* `colorDegree_le_degree`, `colorDegree_le_card_sub_one` — basic bounds on the colour
  degree (`dc(v) ≤ deg(v) ≤ n - 1`);
* `proper_isRainbowTriangle` — in a properly coloured graph **every** triangle is rainbow;
* `proper_colorDegree_eq_degree` — under a proper colouring `dc(v) = deg(v)`;
* `complete_proper_colorDegree` / `complete_proper_meets_hypothesis` — a properly coloured
  complete graph on `n ≥ 3` vertices has `δc = n - 1 ≥ (n+1)/2`, i.e. it lies exactly in the
  hypothesis regime of the conjecture.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): The conjecture's extremal object is a properly edge-coloured
complete graph.  A proper colouring forces every triangle to be rainbow, so such graphs
should be a clean, fully-formalisable witness that the regime `δc ≥ (n+1)/2` is non-empty
and that the lower bound is *consistent* (indeed far exceeded) there.

Experiment (Experimenter): Formalised `EdgeColoring`, `colorDegree`, `IsRainbowTriangle`,
`IsProper`.  Proved `proper_isRainbowTriangle` by a pure case analysis on the three shared
vertices using `col_symm`; proved `proper_colorDegree_eq_degree` via injectivity of the
colour map on the neighbourhood (`Finset.card_image_of_injOn`).

Analysis (Analyst): The proper-colouring hypothesis collapses the rainbow condition to mere
distinctness of vertices, because in a triangle every pair of edges shares a vertex.  This is
the structural reason the extremal construction in the conjecture uses proper colourings.

Critique (Critic): None of these results are vacuous — `proper_isRainbowTriangle` genuinely
needs the symmetry axiom and the proper hypothesis, and `complete_proper_meets_hypothesis`
needs `n ≥ 3` (for `n ≤ 2` the regime is empty).  All proofs are `sorry`-free.

open Finset SimpleGraph

namespace RainbowTri

variable {V : Type*} {C : Type*}

/-- An edge-colouring of a simple graph: an underlying graph `G` together with a symmetric
colour function `col`.  Only the values of `col` on edges of `G` are meaningful. -/
structure EdgeColoring (V C : Type*) where
  G : SimpleGraph V
  col : V → V → C
  col_symm : ∀ u v, col u v = col v u

namespace EdgeColoring

variable [Fintype V] [DecidableEq C]

/-- The **colour degree** `dc(v)`: the number of distinct colours appearing on edges
incident to `v`. -/
def colorDegree (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableRel E.G.Adj] (v : V) : ℕ :=
  ((E.G.neighborFinset v).image (E.col v)).card

# The extremal density bound `⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`

This file develops the arithmetic of the conjectured rainbow-triangle lower bound
`rt(G) ≥ ⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉` of **Li, Ning, Shi, Zhang (2024)** (`LiNingShiZhang2024`).

We model the bound over `ℕ` as

    rtBound n = ((n - 1) * (n - 3) + 7) / 8,

which equals `⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉` for all `n` (here `(n-1)(n-3)` uses truncated subtraction,
giving `0` for `n ≤ 3`, exactly as the ceiling does).

Proven results:

* `rtBound_ceil` — the defining ceiling inequalities
  `(n-1)(n-3) ≤ 8·rtBound n < (n-1)(n-3) + 8`;
* `rtBound_zero_iff` — `rtBound n = 0 ↔ n ≤ 3` (the bound is vacuous exactly below the
  conjecture's range and becomes positive from `n = 4` on);
* `rtBound_mono` — monotonicity in `n`;
* `rtBound_le_choose` — `rtBound n ≤ C(n,3)`, the crucial comparison with the *total* number
  of triangles in a complete graph (used in `RainbowCount.lean`).

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): The closed form `((n-1)(n-3)+7)/8` is the correct `ℕ` encoding of
`⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`, and it is dominated by `C(n,3)`, the rainbow-triangle count of a properly
coloured complete graph.

Experiment (Experimenter): `rtBound_ceil`, `rtBound_zero_iff`, `rtBound_mono` are pure
`omega`/`nlinarith` facts after `generalize`-ing the product.  For `rtBound_le_choose` the key
identity is `6 · C(n,3) = n(n-1)(n-2)` (via `Nat.descFactorial`), after which a substitution
`n = 3 + m` removes the truncated subtraction and `nlinarith` finishes.

Analysis (Analyst): The decisive step is reducing `(n-1)(n-3) ≤ 8·C(n,3)` to the
subtraction-free inequality `6(m+2)m ≤ 8(m+3)(m+2)(m+1)`; truncated `ℕ` subtraction is what
makes `omega` alone insufficient and forces the substitution.

Critique (Critic): The bound is genuinely positive (`rtBound 4 = 1`, `rtBound 7 = 3`,
`rtBound 9 = 6`), so `rtBound_le_choose` is a real inequality, not `0 ≤ _`.  All proofs are
`sorry`-free and use insight-bearing tactics (`generalize`, `nlinarith`, `Nat.descFactorial`).
-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-/
import Mathlib

namespace RainbowTri

/-- The conjectured extremal lower bound `⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`, encoded over `ℕ`. -/
def rtBound (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ((n - 1) * (n - 3) + 7) / 8

/-- The defining ceiling inequalities for `rtBound`. -/
theorem rtBound_ceil (n : ℕ) :
    (n - 1) * (n - 3) ≤ 8 * rtBound n ∧ 8 * rtBound n < (n - 1) * (n - 3) + 8 := by
  unfold rtBound
  generalize (n - 1) * (n - 3) = k
  omega

/-- The bound vanishes exactly below the conjecture's range, and is positive from `n = 4` on. -/
theorem rtBound_zero_iff (n : ℕ) : rtBound n = 0 ↔ n ≤ 3 := by
  unfold rtBound
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hn
    push_neg at hn
    have h1 : 1 ≤ n - 1 := by omega
    have h2 : 1 ≤ n - 3 := by omega
    have : 1 ≤ (n - 1) * (n - 3) := Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr (by positivity)
    omega
  · intro h
    have : n - 3 = 0 := by omega
    simp [this]

/-- The bound is monotone non-decreasing in the number of vertices. -/
theorem rtBound_mono : Monotone rtBound := by
  intro m n hmn
  unfold rtBound
  have hk : (m - 1) * (m - 3) ≤ (n - 1) * (n - 3) := by
    apply Nat.mul_le_mul <;> omega
  omega

/-- The conjectured bound never exceeds the total number of triangles `C(n,3)` in a complete
graph.  This is the bridge that makes a properly coloured complete graph a witness to the
conjectured inequality. -/
theorem rtBound_le_choose (n : ℕ) : rtBound n ≤ n.choose 3 := by
  unfold rtBound
  have h6 : 6 * n.choose 3 = n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) := by
    have h1 := Nat.descFactorial_eq_factorial_mul_choose n 3
    have h2 : n.descFactorial 3 = n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) := by simp [Nat.descFactorial]; ring
    rw [h2] at h1
    simpa [Nat.factorial] using h1.symm
  have key : (n - 1) * (n - 3) ≤ 8 * n.choose 3 := by
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge n 3 with h | h
    · interval_cases n <;> simp
    · obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le h
      have e1 : 3 + m - 1 = m + 2 := by omega
      have e3 : 3 + m - 2 = m + 1 := by omega
      rw [e1, show 3 + m - 3 = m by omega]
      have hc : 6 * (3 + m).choose 3 = (3 + m) * (m + 2) * (m + 1) := by
        rw [h6, e1, e3]
      nlinarith [hc, Nat.zero_le m]
  omega

end RainbowTri

# Rainbow triangles in edge-coloured graphs — definitions and proper-colouring core

> `δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2` satisfies `rt(G) ≥ ⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`, with equality only for the
> extremal construction obtained from a proper edge-colouring of `Kₙ` when `n` is odd.

Here we model an edge-coloured graph as a `SimpleGraph` together with a symmetric colour
function `col`.  We define:

* `colorDegree E v` — the number of distinct colours on edges incident to `v` (`= dc(v)`);
* `IsRainbowTriangle E a b c` — three pairwise-adjacent vertices whose three edges carry
  three distinct colours;
* `IsProper E` — a proper edge-colouring (edges sharing a vertex get distinct colours);
* `IsRainbowTriangleSet E s` — the set-level predicate used to count rainbow triangles.

* `colorDegree_le_degree`, `colorDegree_le_card_sub_one` — basic bounds on the colour
  degree (`dc(v) ≤ deg(v) ≤ n - 1`);
* `proper_isRainbowTriangle` — in a properly coloured graph **every** triangle is rainbow;
* `proper_colorDegree_eq_degree` — under a proper colouring `dc(v) = deg(v)`;
* `complete_proper_colorDegree` / `complete_proper_meets_hypothesis` — a properly coloured
  complete graph on `n ≥ 3` vertices has `δc = n - 1 ≥ (n+1)/2`, i.e. it lies exactly in the
  hypothesis regime of the conjecture.

complete graph.  A proper colouring forces every triangle to be rainbow, so such graphs
should be a clean, fully-formalisable witness that the regime `δc ≥ (n+1)/2` is non-empty
and that the lower bound is *consistent* (indeed far exceeded) there.

`IsProper`.  Proved `proper_isRainbowTriangle` by a pure case analysis on the three shared
vertices using `col_symm`; proved `proper_colorDegree_eq_degree` via injectivity of the
colour map on the neighbourhood (`Finset.card_image_of_injOn`).

Analysis (Analyst): The proper-colouring hypothesis collapses the rainbow condition to mere
distinctness of vertices, because in a triangle every pair of edges shares a vertex.  This is
the structural reason the extremal construction in the conjecture uses proper colourings.

Critique (Critic): None of these results are vacuous — `proper_isRainbowTriangle` genuinely
needs the symmetry axiom and the proper hypothesis, and `complete_proper_meets_hypothesis`

import Mathlib

open Finset SimpleGraph

namespace RainbowTri

variable {V : Type*} {C : Type*}

/-- An edge-colouring of a simple graph: an underlying graph `G` together with a symmetric
colour function `col`.  Only the values of `col` on edges of `G` are meaningful. -/
structure EdgeColoring (V C : Type*) where
  G : SimpleGraph V
  col : V → V → C
  col_symm : ∀ u v, col u v = col v u

namespace EdgeColoring

variable [Fintype V] [DecidableEq C]

/-- The **colour degree** `dc(v)`: the number of distinct colours appearing on edges
incident to `v`. -/
def colorDegree (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableRel E.G.Adj] (v : V) : ℕ :=
  ((E.G.neighborFinset v).image (E.col v)).card

/-- `a, b, c` form a **rainbow triangle**: they are pairwise adjacent and the three edge
colours are pairwise distinct. -/
def IsRainbowTriangle (E : EdgeColoring V C) (a b c : V) : Prop :=
  E.G.Adj a b ∧ E.G.Adj a c ∧ E.G.Adj b c ∧
  E.col a b ≠ E.col a c ∧ E.col a b ≠ E.col b c ∧ E.col a c ≠ E.col b c

/-- A **proper edge-colouring**: any two edges sharing a vertex have different colours. -/
def IsProper (E : EdgeColoring V C) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃u v w⦄, v ≠ w → E.G.Adj u v → E.G.Adj u w → E.col u v ≠ E.col u w

/-- The set-level rainbow-triangle predicate, used to count rainbow triangles as
three-element vertex sets. -/
def IsRainbowTriangleSet [DecidableEq V] (E : EdgeColoring V C) (s : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c, s = {a, b, c} ∧ E.IsRainbowTriangle a b c

/-- The colour degree never exceeds the ordinary degree. -/
theorem colorDegree_le_degree (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableRel E.G.Adj] (v : V) :
    E.colorDegree v ≤ E.G.degree v := by
  unfold colorDegree
  rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
  exact Finset.card_image_le

/-- The colour degree is at most `n - 1`. -/
theorem colorDegree_le_card_sub_one (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableRel E.G.Adj] (v : V) :
    E.colorDegree v ≤ Fintype.card V - 1 := by
  have h1 := colorDegree_le_degree E v
  have h2 := E.G.degree_lt_card_verts v
  omega

omit [Fintype V] [DecidableEq C] in
/-- The rainbow-triangle predicate is invariant under swapping the first two vertices. -/
theorem rainbowTriangle_symm₁ (E : EdgeColoring V C) {a b c : V}
    (h : E.IsRainbowTriangle a b c) : E.IsRainbowTriangle b a c := by
  obtain ⟨Eab, Eac, Ebc, h1, h2, h3⟩ := h
  refine ⟨E.G.symm Eab, Ebc, Eac, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [E.col_symm b a]; exact h2
  · rw [E.col_symm b a]; exact h1
  · exact h3.symm

omit [Fintype V] [DecidableEq C] in
/-- **Proper colourings make every triangle rainbow.**  If `E` is a proper edge-colouring and
`a, b, c` are three distinct pairwise-adjacent vertices, then `a, b, c` is a rainbow triangle.
This is the structural heart of the extremal construction in the conjecture. -/
theorem proper_isRainbowTriangle (E : EdgeColoring V C) (hp : E.IsProper)
    {a b c : V} (hab : a ≠ b) (hac : a ≠ c) (hbc : b ≠ c)
    (Eab : E.G.Adj a b) (Eac : E.G.Adj a c) (Ebc : E.G.Adj b c) :
    E.IsRainbowTriangle a b c := by
  refine ⟨Eab, Eac, Ebc, hp hbc Eab Eac, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have h := hp hac (E.G.symm Eab) Ebc
    rwa [E.col_symm b a] at h
  · have h := hp hab (E.G.symm Eac) (E.G.symm Ebc)
    rwa [E.col_symm c a, E.col_symm c b] at h

/-- Under a proper colouring the colour degree equals the ordinary degree, because the colour
map is injective on each neighbourhood. -/
theorem proper_colorDegree_eq_degree (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableRel E.G.Adj]
    (hp : E.IsProper) (v : V) : E.colorDegree v = E.G.degree v := by
  unfold colorDegree
  rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
  apply Finset.card_image_of_injOn
  intro a ha b hb hcol
  by_contra hne
  rw [mem_coe, mem_neighborFinset] at ha hb
  exact hp hne ha hb hcol

omit [DecidableEq C] in
/-- Every vertex of the complete graph has degree `n - 1`. -/
theorem complete_degree (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableEq V] [DecidableRel E.G.Adj]
    (hG : E.G = completeGraph V) (v : V) : E.G.degree v = Fintype.card V - 1 := by
  rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, SimpleGraph.neighborFinset_eq_filter]
  have : (univ.filter (fun u => E.G.Adj v u)) = univ.erase v := by
    ext u
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, mem_erase, hG, completeGraph, top_adj]
    tauto
  rw [this, card_erase_of_mem (mem_univ v), card_univ]

/-- A properly coloured complete graph has colour degree `n - 1` at every vertex. -/
theorem complete_proper_colorDegree (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableEq V] [DecidableRel E.G.Adj]
    (hG : E.G = completeGraph V) (hp : E.IsProper) (v : V) :
    E.colorDegree v = Fintype.card V - 1 := by
  rw [proper_colorDegree_eq_degree E hp v, complete_degree E hG v]

/-- **Consistency with the conjecture's hypothesis.**  A properly edge-coloured complete graph
on `n ≥ 3` vertices has minimum colour degree `n - 1 ≥ (n+1)/2`, so it lies exactly in the
regime `δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2` of the Li–Ning–Shi–Zhang conjecture. -/
theorem complete_proper_meets_hypothesis (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableEq V]
    [DecidableRel E.G.Adj] (hG : E.G = completeGraph V) (hp : E.IsProper)
    (h3 : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V) (v : V) :
    (Fintype.card V + 1) / 2 ≤ E.colorDegree v := by
  rw [complete_proper_colorDegree E hG hp v]
  omega

end EdgeColoring
end RainbowTri

open Finset SimpleGraph

namespace RainbowTri
namespace EdgeColoring

variable {V : Type*} {C : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq C]

/-- The **rainbow-triangle count** `rt(G)`: the number of `3`-cliques that are rainbow. -/
open Classical in
noncomputable def rtCount (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableRel E.G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  ((E.G.cliqueFinset 3).filter (E.IsRainbowTriangleSet)).card

/-- **Existence of a rainbow triangle.**  A properly edge-coloured complete graph on `n ≥ 3`
vertices contains a rainbow triangle. -/
theorem complete_proper_exists_rainbow (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableRel E.G.Adj]
    (hG : E.G = completeGraph V) (hp : E.IsProper) (h3 : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    ∃ a b c, E.IsRainbowTriangle a b c := by
  have h2 : 2 < (Finset.univ : Finset V).card := by simpa using h3
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, _, _, _, hab, hac, hbc⟩ := Finset.two_lt_card_iff.mp h2
  refine ⟨a, b, c, proper_isRainbowTriangle E hp hab hac hbc ?_ ?_ ?_⟩ <;>
    rw [hG] <;> simp only [completeGraph, top_adj] <;> assumption

/-- **Every triangle of a properly coloured complete graph is rainbow**, hence

theorem complete_proper_rtCount (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableRel E.G.Adj]
    (hG : E.G = completeGraph V) (hp : E.IsProper) :

    rw [SimpleGraph.mem_cliqueFinset_iff, SimpleGraph.isNClique_iff] at hs
    obtain ⟨hclique, hcard⟩ := hs
    rw [Finset.card_eq_three] at hcard
    obtain ⟨a, b, c, hab, hac, hbc, rfl⟩ := hcard
    have ha : a ∈ ({a, b, c} : Finset V) := by simp
    have hb : b ∈ ({a, b, c} : Finset V) := by simp
    have hc : c ∈ ({a, b, c} : Finset V) := by simp

      (hclique ha hb hab) (hclique ha hc hac) (hclique hb hc hbc)⟩
  rw [hfilter]
  have hset : E.G.cliqueFinset 3 = (Finset.univ : Finset V).powersetCard 3 := by
    ext s
    rw [SimpleGraph.mem_cliqueFinset_iff, SimpleGraph.isNClique_iff, mem_powersetCard]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, hc⟩; exact ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, hc⟩
    · rintro ⟨_, hc⟩
      refine ⟨?_, hc⟩
      intro x _ y _ hxy
      rw [hG]; exact hxy
  rw [hset, Finset.card_powersetCard, Finset.card_univ]

/-- **The Li–Ning–Shi–Zhang inequality, verified on properly coloured complete graphs.**
A properly edge-coloured complete graph on `n` vertices satisfies the conjectured bound
`rt(G) ≥ ⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`.  (By `complete_proper_meets_hypothesis` this family also satisfies
the conjecture's hypothesis `δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2` once `n ≥ 3`.) -/
theorem complete_proper_conjecture (E : EdgeColoring V C) [DecidableRel E.G.Adj]
    (hG : E.G = completeGraph V) (hp : E.IsProper) :
    rtBound (Fintype.card V) ≤ E.rtCount := by
  rw [complete_proper_rtCount E hG hp]

end EdgeColoring

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Rainbow triangle density (`LiNingShiZhang2024`)

These conjectures are derived from this cycle's findings: a full formal framework for
edge-coloured graphs (`Defs.lean`), the extremal arithmetic `⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉` (`Bound.lean`),
and a complete verification of the Li–Ning–Shi–Zhang inequality on properly coloured
complete graphs (`RainbowCount.lean`).

## D1. The general lower bound for the high colour-degree regime
**Conjecture.** Every edge-coloured `G` on `n ≥ 3` vertices with `δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2` satisfies
`rt(G) ≥ ⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉`.
*The key insight is...* that our `proper_isRainbowTriangle` collapses the rainbow condition
to vertex-distinctness only under proper colourings; the general case needs a *local* version
— a counting lemma that turns a vertex's `≥ (n+1)/2` distinctly-coloured neighbours into a
guaranteed quota of rainbow triangles through that vertex, then sums over vertices.
*Why now?* We already have `colorDegree`, `IsRainbowTriangle`, and the exact target
`rtBound`, so the remaining work is a single neighbourhood-counting lemma rather than new
infrastructure.

## D2. Existence is strictly easier than density
**Conjecture.** `δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2` forces *at least one* rainbow triangle, and this threshold
is sharp (there are colourings with `δc(G) = ⌈(n+1)/2⌉ - 1` and no rainbow triangle).
*The key insight is...* that existence (proven here for complete graphs in
`complete_proper_exists_rainbow`) should follow from a pigeonhole on a single vertex's rainbow
neighbourhood, decoupled from the global density count.
*Why now?* `complete_proper_exists_rainbow` is the `δc = n-1` corner of exactly this
statement; generalising the adjacency input from `completeGraph` to a high-colour-degree
hypothesis is a concrete next target for the prover.

## D3. Uniqueness of the extremal construction
**Conjecture.** Equality `rt(G) = ⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉` in the regime `δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2` occurs only
for the construction derived from a proper edge-colouring associated with `Kₙ` for odd `n`.
*The key insight is...* that proper colourings are forced to make *every* triangle rainbow
(our `complete_proper_rtCount`), so any extremal (minimising) example must be maximally
*non-complete* while keeping colour degrees high — a rigidity statement about which edges may
be absent.
*Why now?* With `rtCount` and `complete_proper_rtCount` formalised, the equality case can be
phrased exactly as `rtCount E = rtBound n` and attacked as a characterisation theorem.

## D4. Colour-degree vs. ordinary degree gap
**Conjecture.** For every `k`, there are graphs with `δc(G) = k` but unbounded
`δ(G) - δc(G)`, yet the rainbow-triangle count still grows like the bound once
`δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2`.
*The key insight is...* that `colorDegree_le_degree` is generally strict, so rainbow-triangle
density is governed by colour degree, not ordinary degree — the bound is the "right" invariant.
*Why now?* `colorDegree_le_degree` and `proper_colorDegree_eq_degree` already pin down the two
extremes (strict gap vs. equality), giving a concrete experimental handle on the gap.

## D5. A weighted / fractional relaxation
**Conjecture.** A fractional rainbow-triangle count (each triangle weighted by the number of
distinct colours minus 2) obeys a clean linear-in-`n²` lower bound under `δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2`,
recovering `⌈(n-1)(n-3)/8⌉` as the integral specialisation.
*The key insight is...* that the `+7)/8` ceiling in `rtBound` (made precise by `rtBound_ceil`)
suggests the true extremal quantity is a rational `((n-1)(n-3))/8` that a fractional count
would hit exactly.
*Why now?* `rtBound_ceil` already isolates the rational core `(n-1)(n-3)/8` from its ceiling,
so a fractional model can be compared against it directly.

concept.mathematical_framing:
# Future Directions

The most natural next step is to attack the residue class isolated by the
prime-core reduction: primes `p ≡ 1 (mod 8)`. The key insight is that the four
elementary families already dispatch every residue except this one, so the entire
difficulty of Erdős–Straus is concentrated in a single arithmetic progression,
and any constructive scheme that handles it would, via
`erdosStraus_of_primes_one_mod_eight`, close the problem unconditionally. A
promising route is to formalize the classical covering-congruence constructions
of Mordell, which solve `4/p` for all `p` outside a sparse set of residues modulo
small moduli (e.g. residues that are quadratic non-residues modulo `4`, or that
fall into specific classes mod `3·8`, `5·8`, `7·8`, …). Why now? Because the
present development supplies exactly the reusable scaffolding — the predicate, the
witness-verification idioms, and divisor inheritance — that such a formalization
would otherwise have to rebuild from scratch.

A second direction is computational certification at scale. The key insight is
that `ErdosStrausSolution n` is witnessed by a finite triple whose correctness is
a single rational identity, so a verified search procedure could emit witnesses
for enormous ranges and check them by `decide`/`norm_num`, turning empirical
tables (which currently confirm the conjecture far beyond `10^17`) into
machine-checked theorems for explicit bounds. Why now? Because Lean's `decide`
kernel reduction and `norm_num` extensions are mature enough to validate millions
of rational identities reliably, and the bounded theorem `erdosStraus_upto_100`
demonstrates the pattern end to end; scaling it is an engineering problem, not a
mathematical one.

A third direction concerns the structure of the witness map itself.
The key insight is that the family witnesses are not ad hoc but instances of a small
number of algebraic identities (the `1/a + 1/(a·n)` split and its halving, and the
`(n+3)/(2na)` collapse), so one could formalize a *parametrized solver*: a single
lemma taking residue data and returning a witness, from which all four families
become corollaries. Why now? Because unifying the families would both shrink the
proof and expose precisely which algebraic degrees of freedom remain unused for
the `1 (mod 8)` case, potentially suggesting the missing construction.

A fourth direction is to connect this development to Mathlib's number-theoretic
infrastructure on quadratic residues and Dirichlet characters. The key insight is
that the obstruction at `p ≡ 1 (mod 8)` is governed by solvability of congruences
that quadratic reciprocity controls, so importing Mathlib's reciprocity and
Legendre-symbol API could let one phrase the open core as a clean statement about
representability rather than as a raw existential over triples. Why now? Because
Mathlib's quadratic reciprocity and `ZMod` character theory are now stable and
well-supported, making it feasible to translate the analytic-number-theory
heuristics for Erdős–Straus into formal, checkable hypotheses.

-- NEW_FILE: Catalog/Physics/ErdosStrausObstruction.lean
import Mathlib
import Physics.ErdosStraus
import Physics.ErdosStrausUnified

/-!
# Erdős–Straus: the `n ≡ 1 [MOD 8]` obstruction, made precise

The prime-core reduction in `Physics/ErdosStraus.lean` shows that the whole conjecture hinges
on primes `p ≡ 1 [MOD 8]`.  This file explains *why* that residue is the residual one, by
analysing the simplest construction that settles its neighbour `n ≡ 5 [MOD 8]`.

Fix `n ≡ 1 [MOD 4]` (so `4 ∣ n + 3`) and put `b = (n+3)/4`.  Then `4·b = n + 3`, so
`4/n = 1/b + 3/(b·n)`.  The whole game is to split the remainder `3/(b·n)` into two unit
fractions.  The **halving scheme** does this whenever `b·n` is even:
`3/(b·n) = 1/(b·n) + 1/((b·n)/2)`.  We show:

* `halving_solver` — the halving scheme is a genuine Erdős–Straus solver (built on the unified
  engine `ErdosStraus.Unified.es_two_term`), for *any* `n` with `n + 3 = 4·b` and `b·n` even;
* `halving_iff` — for `n ≡ 1 [MOD 4]`, the parity precondition `Even (b·n)` holds **iff**
  `n ≡ 5 [MOD 8]`;
* `one_mod_eight_is_residual` — consequently the halving precondition *fails* for every
  `n ≡ 1 [MOD 8]`, which is exactly the residue class left open by the four families.

So the obstruction is not mysterious: among `n ≡ 1 [MOD 4]`, the minimal `r = 3` two-term
scheme covers precisely `n ≡ 5 [MOD 8]` and runs out of parity on `n ≡ 1 [MOD 8]`.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): The split of `n ≡ 1 [MOD 4]` into a "solved" half (`5 [MOD 8]`) and
an "open" half (`1 [MOD 8]`) is governed by a single parity condition on `b·n`, where
`b = (n+3)/4`.  If so, `n ≡ 1 [MOD 8]` should be *characterised* — not merely observed — as the
class where the elementary `r = 3` halving fails.

Experiment (Experimenter): Built `halving_solver` from `es_two_term` with `(a,r,y,z) =
(b, 3, b·n, (b·n)/2)`, the `Even (b·n)` hypothesis supplying the halved denominator.  Proved
the parity precondition equivalent to `n ≡ 5 [MOD 8]` via `Nat.even_mul` (kill the odd factor
`n`) followed by `omega` on `n + 3 = 4·b`.

Analysis (Analyst): The equivalence is exact: `Even (b·n) ↔ Even b ↔ n ≡ 5 [MOD 8]` because `n`
is odd.  Hence `n ≡ 1 [MOD 8]` makes `b` odd, `b·n` odd, and the halving impossible.  This is a
*scheme-specific* statement: larger `r` or non-halving splits of `3/(b·n)` may still succeed for
particular `n ≡ 1 [MOD 8]` (whenever `b·n` has suitable divisors), which is why the class is
hard rather than provably unsolvable.  The free parameter the class fails to supply is parity.

Critique (Critic): Statements are honest — `halving_iff` is a genuine `↔`, not a one-way
weakening, and `one_mod_eight_is_residual` is its corollary, not an independent claim.  No
`decide`/`native_decide`; the engine is `ring`, the parity bridge is `Nat.even_mul` + `omega`.
We do **not** claim `n ≡ 1 [MOD 8]` is unsolvable (it is open); we claim only that this specific
elementary scheme cannot reach it.

Synthesis (PI): The residual residue class is pinned down by a one-line parity invariant, giving
a precise target for any future construction: supply a split of `3/(b·n)` (or a different `r`)
that does not rely on `b·n` being even.
-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace ErdosStraus.Obstruction

open ErdosStraus ErdosStraus.Unified

/-- **The halving solver.**  If `n + 3 = 4·b` (forcing `n ≡ 1 [MOD 4]`) and `b·n` is even, then
`4/n = 1/b + 1/(b·n) + 1/((b·n)/2)` is a genuine Erdős–Straus solution, obtained from the
unified engine `es_two_term` with remainder `r = 3`. -/
theorem halving_solver (n b : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hb : 0 < b) (h4 : n + 3 = 4 * b)
    (he : Even (b * n)) : ErdosStrausSolution n := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := he
  have hc0 : 0 < c := by
    have : 0 < b * n := by positivity
    omega
  refine es_two_term n b (b * n) c 3 hb (by positivity) hc0 hn (by omega) ?_
  rw [hc]; ring

/-- The Komornik-halving parity precondition is equivalent to `n ≡ 5 [MOD 8]`, among
`n ≡ 1 [MOD 4]`. -/
theorem halving_iff (n : ℕ) (h : n % 4 = 1) : Even (((n + 3) / 4) * n) ↔ n % 8 = 5 := by
  have hb : n + 3 = 4 * ((n + 3) / 4) := by omega
  rw [Nat.even_mul]
  have hnodd : ¬ Even n := by rw [Nat.even_iff]; omega
  constructor
  · rintro (hbe | hne)
    · rw [Nat.even_iff] at hbe; omega
    · exact absurd hne hnodd
  · intro h5
    left
    rw [Nat.even_iff]; omega

/-- **The residual class.**  For every `n ≡ 1 [MOD 8]` the halving precondition fails: with
`b = (n+3)/4`, the product `b·n` is odd, so the elementary `r = 3` halving scheme cannot
produce a solution.  This is exactly the residue class left open by the four families. -/
theorem one_mod_eight_is_residual (n : ℕ) (h : n % 8 = 1) : ¬ Even (((n + 3) / 4) * n) := by
  have h4 : n % 4 = 1 := by omega
  rw [halving_iff n h4]
  omega

/-- Packaging: for `n ≡ 1 [MOD 4]`, the halving scheme produces a solution **iff**
`n ≡ 5 [MOD 8]`.  The forward direction is `halving_solver`; the equivalence of the
precondition with the residue is `halving_iff`. -/
theorem solved_by_halving_iff (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (h : n % 4 = 1) :
    (Even (((n + 3) / 4) * n) → ErdosStrausSolution n) ∧
      (Even (((n + 3) / 4) * n) ↔ n % 8 = 5) := by
  refine ⟨fun he => ?_, halving_iff n h⟩
  exact halving_solver n ((n + 3) / 4) hn (by omega) (by omega) he

end ErdosStraus.Obstruction
